answer.new_information: NVIDIA's own 2026-07-01 announcement of a new business model: AI clouds procure NVIDIA infrastructure for AI-native, enterprise and ISV customers under a revenue-sharing and credit-support model, with NVIDIA earning standard product revenue plus a share of cloud revenue on supported capacity. No amounts, capacity commitments, credit-support size, counterparties' terms, or period are disclosed. The Sharon AI and Firmus items are CEO quotes and NVIDIA's description of a planned Batam campus (expected to scale to 360 MW and up to 170,000 GPUs), all carried in the same NVIDIA release and not yet delivered.
answer.new_question: Does NVIDIA's revenue-sharing and credit-support model for AI clouds add contingent financial exposure and circular revenue dependence on a small set of capital-constrained AI cloud counterparties?
answer.independent_judgement: Treat the model as a shift of NVDA's economics toward a usage-linked revenue stream plus credit exposure to AI clouds. Watch for disclosed credit-support size, counterparty concentration, and whether recognized revenue depends on NVIDIA-backed financing. Until sized, the view is a risk and earnings-quality question, not a change to forecast revenue.
answer.reason: No catalog questions or stored pieces exist to update. The record carries an investment judgement (credit exposure and circularity from the model) that no catalog question covers and that could change the position view. The record has no sizes or terms, so it does not move any number and is not a background pickup.
